preamble: Proto-Celtic *w became /f/ word-initially in Goidelic, whereas Brythonic changed it to gw-. The change affected inherited vocabulary (Proto-Celtic *wiros 'man' > Old Irish fer, Welsh gŵr) and early Latin loans whose v was still [w] (vīnum > Old Irish fín). It is an initial fortition with devoicing that is well established in Celtic but rare elsewhere.

examples.to: fer; Irish fear, Scottish Gaelic fear
examples.note: Contrast Brythonic Welsh gŵr from the same etymon.

sources: Stifter, D. (2006). Sengoídelc: Old Irish for Beginners. Syracuse University Press.
McManus, D. (1991). A Guide to Ogam. Maynooth Monographs 4. An Sagart.
